# RETRO: omacom/omarchy#12503

## What worked
- Naming the dependency source (CUPS, cups-browsed, Arch packaging) in the brief let both reviewers reach the same central finding independently. The PKGBUILD configure flags were decisive for likelihood.
- One targeted Sol follow-up turned two single-sourced public claims (message breadth, earlier design history) into independently confirmed ones in about 5 minutes.
- The editorial check passed on the first draft.

## Friction and deviations
- `pi_job.py wait` prints the job's `latest_text`, so Sol's one-line closing summary was shown to the coordinator before the Opus final existed. It was not shared with Opus. Suggestion: have `wait` omit `latest_text` (or offer a `--lifecycle-only` flag).
- Opus used `cut -c` once on its own fixture file (not a source or policy read). Self-reported.
- Opus's first Arch GitLab fetch for cups missed the epoch in the tag (`2-2.4.19-1`) and got a 404, which it discarded. Future briefs could note epoch-prefixed tags.
- The subagent prompt follows the system-prompt rule (brief path only). First-call rules therefore reached Opus via the brief file, not the dispatch text. That conflicts with the older PR13009 dispatch rule. No read deviation resulted beyond the `cut -c` note.
- The `review.py init` inside-output-dir rule led Opus to build subset Git repos. Blob IDs match upstream, so provenance is preserved.

## Tool notes
- No confirmed tool bugs. Feature request: a lifecycle-only mode for `pi_job.py wait`/`status`.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the new condition matches the real CUPS 2.4.19 output and stops migration `1788009111` from aborting `omarchy update` when `lpstat -v` cannot reach the scheduler. In CUPS 2.4.19, `show_devices()` in `systemv/lpstat.c` prints exactly `lpstat: Scheduler is not running.` and exits 1 in that case, and the string has no translation in any CUPS catalog, so the exact match is locale-independent. Other `lpstat -v` errors still exit 1. In an isolated run of the migration with stubbed `lpstat`, `sudo`, `pacman` and `systemctl`, the results were:

| Stubbed `lpstat -v` result | Base | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `lpstat: Scheduler is not running.`, exit 1 | exit 1, package kept, no marker | exit 0, package dropped, marker written |
| `lpstat: No destinations added.`, exit 1 | exit 0, package dropped, marker written | unchanged |
| `lpstat: Forbidden`, exit 1 | exit 1, package kept, no marker | unchanged |
| one `implicitclass://` queue and one USB queue | 2 queue actions, exit 0 | unchanged |

One side effect of the new branch is worth a look.

### Scheduler-unavailable path marks discovery cleanup complete without checking for saved queues

With the new branch, an unreachable scheduler is read as an empty queue list. The migration then removes the backend that any discovery queues depend on and records itself as permanently complete:

```text
lpstat -v -> "lpstat: Scheduler is not running."
  -> queue_report=""                  (no cupsreject / lpstat -o / lpadmin -x)
  -> omarchy-pkg-drop cups-browsed    (removes the implicitclass backend)
  -> machine marker written           (migration exits early on every later run)

later: cupsd starts
  -> loads saved implicitclass queues from /etc/cups/printers.conf
  -> backend missing: queue stopped, cannot print
```

The later cupsd steps come from CUPS 2.4.19 and cups-browsed 2.1.1 source (`scheduler/printers.c` loads saved queues and stops any whose backend is missing). They were not reproduced with a real CUPS instance.

This reverses an earlier explicit choice in this migration. Commit `24c18df5` captures the queue list "so a cupsd it cannot reach is reported instead of reading like a machine with nothing to clean up". The migration's shell test at `96d56824` (removed in `2002fb35`) required an unavailable CUPS server to leave the package installed and write no marker. `agents/skills/migrations.md` also says a migration that cannot finish must exit non-zero and remain pending.

The matched message is also broader than "stopped". libcups reports it for any service-unavailable result: a refused connection, a connection timeout to an unresponsive cupsd, an unreachable configured server, or HTTP errors without a specific mapping (`cups/request.c`, `_cupsConnect` and `_cupsSetHTTPError`).

**Impact:** on a machine that still has saved `implicitclass://` queues while the scheduler is unreachable, those queues reappear as stopped printers the next time CUPS starts, and this migration never revisits them. Leftovers should be uncommon. Arch builds cups-browsed 2.1.1 without `--enable-saving-created-queues`, so a cups-browsed that stops cleanly while CUPS is reachable deletes its own idle queues. Leftovers remain possible after `KeepGeneratedQueuesOnShutdown Yes`, or after a cups-browsed exit that skipped its cleanup.

**Suggested change:** check the saved configuration before treating the message as an empty list, for example with `sudo grep -q '^DeviceURI implicitclass:' /etc/cups/printers.conf` (the file is root-only). If no discovery queues are saved, proceed as this PR does. If some are, keep the migration pending with a message that explains how to resolve it, or start CUPS only for the cleanup. This check is an untested suggestion. At minimum, printing a line when queue cleanup is skipped would make the path visible; the PR's version is silent.

**Documentation note:** the comment above the branch (lines 23-25) still describes only "A healthy CUPS server with no configured printers" and could mention the scheduler-unavailable case.

**Related:** open PR #12101 contains the same `Scheduler is not running.` condition.
